newsitem.title: BRAZIL: ACPC members to start discussing export cut plan.
newsitem.headline: ACPC members to start discussing export cut plan.

text.p: Members of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) will begin technical discussions on Wednesday on an African proposal to reduce ACPC member exports in the first half of this year, producer officials said.
"These will be technical discussions prior to the ACPC meeting to be held tomorrow," an African producer official said.
This follows speculation that a recent rise in arabica and, more recently, robusta prices might reduce the need to cut exports by the proposed 2.5 million bags.
However, producer officials declined to comment prior to their full meeting on January 23.
"I have no opinion yet, we are waiting for the figures from the ACPC," said Jorge Cardenas, head of Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation.
Cardenas said ACPC members had discussed reducing exports at their last meeting in Costa Rica in November but pointed out that the market situation had changed since then.
"We want to do a professional job but we have to take into account the new reality in terms of size of crop, demand and supply," Cardenas said. "Since the middle of December we have new information."
